evidence.claim: Joshua trees, dry lake beds and mountain ranges along a desert highway.
evidence.quote: From Route 66 in Barstow to Yucca Valley, travelers will pass through the Ord Mountains, Lucerne Dry Lake, Homestead Valley, Black Lava Butte, and Flattop Mesa.

evidence.claim: Joshua trees
evidence.quote: along with Joshua trees, creosote bush, cholla cacti, and yucca.

evidence.claim: Route 247 crosses the Mojave Desert between Barstow and Yucca Valley, using Barstow Road and Old Woman Springs Road.
evidence.quote: The road passes through the Mojave Desert in San Bernardino County, connecting SR 62 in Yucca Valley to Interstate 15 (I-15) in Barstow. SR 247 runs along Old Woman Springs Road between Yucca Valley to Lucerne Valley, and Barstow Road between Lucerne Valley and Barstow.

evidence.claim: The two-lane Old Woman Springs section parallels the north side of the San Bernardino Mountains through Johnson Valley.
evidence.quote: From Yucca Valley, the two-lane highway heads northwestward through desert and parallels the north side of the San Bernardino Mountains, much of it through Johnson Valley

evidence.claim: Caltrans designated the Barstow-to-Yucca Valley corridor a scenic byway in 2025.
evidence.quote: SACRAMENTO, Calif., Oct. 4, 2025 — Scenic America is thrilled to share that the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) has officially designated State Route 247 — the stretch from Barstow to Yucca Valley — as the state’s newest scenic byway.

evidence.claim: Joshua trees, creosote and cholla grow along a corridor of mesas, sand washes, lava flows and mountain ranges.
evidence.quote: Natural features include the Blackhawk landslide — a prehistoric mountain collapse — along with Joshua trees, creosote bush, cholla cacti, and yucca. The corridor also showcases mesas, sand washes, lava flows, cinder cones, mountain ranges

evidence.claim: In 1964, the Lucerne Valley Chamber of Commerce began campaigning for a state highway along Old Woman Springs Road between Lucerne Valley and Yucca Valley.
evidence.quote: That year, the Lucerne Valley Chamber of Commerce began an effort to have a state highway designated from Lucerne Valley to Yucca Valley along Old Woman Springs Road.

evidence.claim: By 1969, county roads connected Barstow, Lucerne Valley and Yucca Valley.
evidence.quote: By 1969, county roads had been constructed from Barstow to Lucerne Valley, and from there to Yucca Valley.

evidence.claim: San Bernardino County transferred Barstow Road and Old Woman Springs Road to the state in 1972, while agreeing to carry out further improvements after state maintenance began.
evidence.quote: Barstow Road and Old Woman Springs Road were given to the state by San Bernardino County in 1972, although the county had agreed to perform some improvements on the two roads after the state began to maintain them.
SR 247 was designated in the 1964 state highway renumbering

evidence.claim: Driving south from Barstow takes you through the Ord Mountains and past Lucerne Dry Lake toward Lucerne Valley.
evidence.quote: From Route 66 in Barstow to Yucca Valley, travelers will pass through the Ord Mountains, Lucerne Dry Lake, Homestead Valley, Black Lava Butte, and Flattop Mesa.

evidence.claim: There, follow Old Woman Springs Road southeast through Johnson Valley and the western tip of Landers.
evidence.quote: From Yucca Valley, the two-lane highway heads northwestward through desert and parallels the north side of the San Bernardino Mountains, much of it through Johnson Valley, briefly passing through Flamingo Heights and the western tip of Landers.

evidence.claim: Flamingo Heights comes before the final junction with Route 62 in Yucca Valley.
evidence.quote: SR 247 begins at a junction with SR 62 in the town of Yucca Valley, where it is signed as Old Woman Springs Road.  From Yucca Valley, the two-lane highway heads northwestward through desert and parallels the north side of the San Bernardino Mountains, much of it through Johnson Valley, briefly passing through Flamingo Heights and the western tip of Landers.

evidence.claim: The Ord Mountains run generally east to west, with Ord Mountain rising to 6,309 feet.
evidence.quote: The range lies in a generally east–west direction, and reaches an elevation of 6,309 feet (1,923 m) above sea level at Ord Mountain.

evidence.claim: The range is approximately 14 miles long and lies southeast of Barstow, above North Lucerne Valley.
evidence.quote: The range is approximately 14 miles (23 km) long, 15 mi (24 km) northeast of Apple Valley and 19 mi (31 km) miles southeast of Barstow.

evidence.claim: These mountains belonged to the Ord Mountain Mining District in the late nineteenth century.
evidence.quote: In the late 1800s, the area was part of the Ord Mountain Mining District.

evidence.claim: In the early twentieth century, miners extracted about 500 tons of gold and silver ore; copper mining followed during the World Wars.
evidence.quote: In the early 1900s, about 500 tons of gold and silver ore were mined, and copper was mined during the World Wars.

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Land Management administers the area, and the Ord Mountain Trail passes through one section of the range.
evidence.quote: The area is administered by the Bureau of Land Management. The Ord Mountain Trail goes through one section of the mountains.

evidence.claim: above North Lucerne Valley.
evidence.quote: to the south is the North Lucerne Valley;

evidence.claim: Lucerne Lake is a dry lake bed in the Mojave Desert, 15 miles east of Apple Valley.
evidence.quote: Lucerne Lake is a dry lake bed  in the Mojave Desert of San Bernardino County, California, 24 km (15 mi) east of Apple Valley.

evidence.claim: It measures approximately 3.7 miles long and 5 miles at its widest point.
evidence.quote: The lake is approximately 6 km (3.7 mi) long and 8 km (5.0 mi) at its widest point.

evidence.claim: Small meteorites have been found here and at nearby Rabbit Springs Dry Lake.
evidence.quote: Lucerne Dry Lake and Rabbit Springs Dry Lake — two dry lakes in the Lucerne Valley. A variety of small meteorites have been found in these two dry lakes.

evidence.claim: Landers grew from gold prospecting at Goat Mountain, beginning with Charles Reche in 1914.
evidence.quote: The Landers area was originally settled in the early 20th century by prospectors who came to mine gold in Goat Mountain, starting with Charles Reche in 1914.

evidence.claim: From the late 1940s through the 1970s, UFO enthusiasts gathered for conventions focused on Giant Rock and the Integratron.
evidence.quote: From the late 1940s through the 1970s, Landers was a popular gathering point for conventions of UFO enthusiasts, with the primary destinations of interest being the Integratron and nearby Giant Rock.

evidence.claim: George Van Tassel built the Integratron between 1957 and 1977.
evidence.quote: Author, inventor, and UFO advocate George Van Tassel (1910–1978) built the Integratron structure in the Giant Rock area from 1957 to 1977.

evidence.claim: Its wooden dome uses 16 laminated spines held together at the top by a ton of concrete.
evidence.quote: The Integratron dome is built using a unique design of wood construction with 16 glued and laminated spines held together at its apex by one ton of concrete.

evidence.claim: North of Landers, remains of Giant Rock’s packed-sand airstrip and a concrete cafe pad survive from Van Tassel’s activities there.
evidence.quote: The deteriorated remains of a packed sand air strip that was operational from 1947 to 1975 are still visible, as is a concrete pad that was the location of a cafe at the site, built and operated by George Van Tassel, who also built the Integratron.

evidence.claim: North of Landers
evidence.quote: Adjacent to Landers on the north is Giant Rock

evidence.claim: Joshua trees, creosote bush, cholla and yucca are among the corridor’s desert plants.
evidence.quote: along with Joshua trees, creosote bush, cholla cacti, and yucca.

evidence.claim: Before state ownership, the corridor carried miners and freight heading for the Dale District east of Twentynine Palms, then homesteaders arriving after World War II.
evidence.quote: The corridor later carried miners and freight bound for the Dale District east of Twentynine Palms and eventually carried post‑World War II homesteaders seeking new opportunities in the high desert.

evidence.claim: In the early twentieth century, miners extracted about 500 tons of gold and silver ore; copper mining followed during the World Wars.
evidence.quote: In the early 1900s, about 500 tons of gold and silver ore were mined, and copper was mined during the World Wars.

evidence.claim: Landers lies in Homestead Valley, north of Yucca Valley and Flamingo Heights.
evidence.quote: Landers lies in the Homestead Valley of the southeastern Mojave Desert.

evidence.claim: north of Yucca Valley and Flamingo Heights.
evidence.quote: Landers is 14 miles (23 km) north of Yucca Valley, and borders the community of Flamingo Heights to its south.
